shared.surfBiteReport: Note: The most current readable report found for this stretch is from noeoutdoors.com/pcb, posted approximately three weeks ago (mid-July 2026) — so treat this as recent but not this week's data. At 84°F water temps, the surf bite along the PCB and 30A beaches has been steady, particularly in the early morning and the last couple of hours before sunset; mid-day heat pushes fish deeper or slows them considerably. Spanish mackerel and whiting are the most consistent producers right now, with mackerel chasing baitfish schools tight to the beaches and whiting responding well to sand fleas, shrimp, and Fishbites fished in the deeper troughs between sandbars rather than cast to the horizon. Redfish and jack crevalle have also been showing up along the beach face, and baitfish are thick along the shoreline — when birds start working or bait starts jumping, that's your signal to move and cast into that zone fast.
